title: Crispy Honey Chili Eggs
subtitle: Sheet-pan hash with eggs cracked over the top.
description: Potatoes, sausage, and peppers roasted on a sheet pan with eggs cracked over the top in the oven. One pan, easy cleanup, feeds ten.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crispy Honey Chili Eggs in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use olive oil or bacon fat, shredded cheddar as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Line a full sheet pan with parchment or foil for easy cleanup. Allow 10–15 minutes for mise en place before heat goes on. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Roast the hash base
steps.instruction: Toss potatoes with oil, salt, and pepper. Spread in one layer and roast 15 minutes. Add sausage, onion, and peppers; roast until potatoes are browned and sausage is hot. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Make wells for eggs
steps.instruction: Pull pan from oven. Make shallow wells across the hash. Crack eggs into wells and season lightly. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Bake until eggs set
steps.instruction: Return to oven until whites are set and yolks are still slightly soft (or longer for firm yolks). Finish with cheese if using. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

stationWorkflow: Assign one cook to the hot surface and one to assembly. Keep the line moving; don’t crowd the griddle.
Set a warm holding zone (oven 200°F or covered hotel pan) so staggered eaters still get a hot plate.
Run a quick call-proof check: anything crispy stays uncovered; anything soft stays covered.
cleanupNotes: While plates are served, scrape the griddle/pan and wipe with a damp towel (use tongs + folded towel).
Soak the mixing bowl and sheet pan immediately—breakfast starch sets fast when it cools.
leftovers: Cool fast: spread on a sheet pan 10 minutes, then portion into containers so it doesn’t sweat.
Reheat rule: eggs reheat best covered at 50% power or low oven heat; don’t nuke on high.
